title: Bring it to the right person with a proposed mitigation
why_matters: Raising a risk without a proposed mitigation is reporting; raising one with a mitigation is contributing. The mitigation doesn't have to be the right one — it has to be specific enough that the person who owns the response can either say yes or counter-propose. This is the move that turns a risk from a worry into work.
steps: Take the risk you surfaced. Identify the person who'd own the response — usually a different person from who'd be affected.
Write a short paragraph: the risk in one sentence, the proposed mitigation in two, the cost in one.
Book a fifteen-minute conversation. Don't email and wait; the writing is for the conversation, not instead of it.
After the conversation, write up what was agreed (mitigation accepted, modified, or declined with reason) and add it to the RAID log.
success_criteria: A fifteen-minute conversation has happened with the response owner. The RAID log entry has been updated with the decision (accepted, modified, or declined + reason). You can name the next concrete step.
reflection_prompt: What was the response you didn't expect, and what does it tell you about how this organisation handles risk?
